intro: This taxonomy maps the kinds of things a person owns for everyday life and for their hobbies. Read it from the top down: ten domains group neighbouring categories; each category has departments and shelves; shelves hold kinds (generic types of object, such as a chef's knife or a field jacket); a collected kind runs on to named archetypes (an icon, pattern or model family) and their versions (generations, editions, reissues, reproductions).

Each department is marked with a mode. Variety means people explore and collect many makers, so every notable maker and named form is listed, with the long tail as short entries. Tier means people want to pick a good one, so the list keeps the makers that cover most of the market and the ones that top independent tests. Mixed means tier for the everyday end and variety for the enthusiast end.

Every object has one home. To find it, answer the questions of the placement key in order and stop at the first yes. Cross-links point to neighbouring homes and to related taxonomies (entertainment titles, pursuits, dishes); they never give an object a second home.
Makers, craft traditions, scenes, periods and other registers are separate views over the same objects: they help you browse, but they never decide where an object lives.
key: 1. Outside the scope of this taxonomy (a one-off service or single-event ticket, a bank or crypto balance, a title, a genre, a pursuit, a dish or recipe, trade-only equipment)? → not filed
2. A living animal, not sold alive to be eaten? → breeds and species register (no category)

3. Made to diagnose, treat, monitor or compensate for an illness, injury or disability, or for contraception, fertility, pregnancy, breastfeeding or first aid, and not built into the home? → H2 Health, Medical & Mobility
4. A living plant, fungus or culture, a fresh-cut ornamental plant or tree, or a seed, bulb, spore or cutting for growing? → C3 Plants & Living Cultures
5. Tobacco, nicotine, cannabis or another plant product taken for its effect, or gear made to smoke, vape or store it? → J10 Smoking & Vaping
6. An alcoholic drink in a sealed container, or a no- or low-alcohol version of beer, wine, cider or spirits? → J7 Wine, Beer & Spirits
7. A ready-to-drink soft drink, bottled water, juice, cordial or drink syrup, fermented soft drink, energy or sports drink, or ready-to-drink coffee or tea? → J9 Soft Drinks & Water
8. Coffee, tea, cocoa or another plant infusion bought to brew or mix at home? → J6 Coffee, Tea & Cocoa
9. Bread or other baked goods, biscuits, crackers, chocolate, sweets, crisps and savoury snacks, nuts, snack bars or ice cream? → J8 Bakery, Sweets & Snacks
10. Meat, poultry or game in any form, a meat product, or a meat alternative? → J1 Meat & Poultry
11. Fish or seafood in any form, live shellfish sold to eat included? → J2 Fish & Seafood
12. Milk, cream, butter, yoghurt, cheese, eggs, infant formula, or a plant alternative to them, or tofu, tempeh or yuba? → J3 Dairy, Eggs & Alternatives
13. Fresh fruit, vegetables, salad, herbs, mushrooms or sea vegetables, sold to eat? → J4 Fruit & Vegetables
14. Any other food bought to eat or cook with, packaged prepared foods included? → J5 Pantry Staples
15. Land, a dwelling or estate as a whole, a home that floats or is factory-built, or a burial place? → G2 Property & Structures
16. Built into or fixed to a home or its grounds as part of it, or a home system (heating, water, power, controls), or a sauna or hot tub of any kind? → G3 Home Fixtures & Features
17. Software: a program, app or hosted tool valued for what it does? → I1 Software
18. An item that exists only as data (font, creative asset, game or platform item, personal media file, domain, NFT)? → I2 Digital Media & Items
19. A subscription, membership, pass, connectivity plan, online utility service, recurring delivery or retained service? → I3 Subscriptions, Memberships & Online Services
20. A natural object, not made by people beyond cleaning, cutting or preserving, kept as a specimen? → F6 Natural History & Specimens
21. A part, attachment, case or consumable made for one kind of object? → the category of that object
22. Made for sexual stimulation or for restraint in sexual activity, or for their care? → H3 Adult Objects
23. A weapon for fighting, self-defence, hunting or target shooting, its ammunition, sights or parts, armour, or a deactivated or replica weapon? → E4 Weapons & Armour
24. Made mainly to move people or goods, a motorcycle rider's helmet or gear, or a product made for vehicle care? → G1 Vehicles
25. Farm, smallholding or woodland machinery or livestock equipment? → C7 Farm & Forestry Equipment
26. Made to keep, feed, house, carry, train or care for animals? → B10 Animal Equipment
27. Made for worship, devotion, divination or mourning, or as ceremonial regalia or insignia of office? → F4 Religious & Ceremonial Objects
28. Money, bullion, a stamp or postal item, a trading card, token, medal, decoration or trophy, or a holder or album made for them? → F3 Coins, Stamps, Medals & Trading Cards

29. A personal or collected paper or card: a letter, autograph, manuscript, photograph, postcard, ephemera, share, payment or transit card, identity or legal document? → F5 Documents & Personal Records
30. An original or editioned work of art, or a collectible figurine made as an ornament? → F2 Art
31. A published work on a physical carrier (book, record, disc, tape, film, comic, periodical, sheet music, map, globe), or storage made for such media? → F1 Media & Publications
32. Video-game hardware, game media as objects, a VR or XR headset, or an arcade or pinball machine? → E5 Video Games
33. A musical instrument or gear for making, amplifying, recording or DJing music? → E3 Musical Instruments & Music Gear
34. Made to observe the sky, nature or the very small, or to measure weather and the Earth, for study or hobby? → E6 Observing & Measuring
35. A computer, its components, storage, peripherals, printers, networking, cables or maker electronics? → D1 Computers & Components
36. A phone, tablet, e-reader, wearable, organiser, navigator or tracker, or a two-way or amateur radio? → D2 Phones, Tablets & Personal Devices
37. Equipment for listening to sound or watching pictures (headphones, speakers, hi-fi, radio, TV, projector, players, smart speakers)? → D3 Audio & Video
38. A camera, lens or other equipment for taking or making photographs and video? → D4 Cameras & Photography
39. A watch, clock or timer made to show or measure time? → A5 Clocks & Watches
40. Made for play, or for a game played at a table or with cards, dice, tiles or tokens, or a hobby model? → E1 Toys & Games
41. Made for a sport, fitness, dance or outdoor recreation, including garments, footwear and helmets made for one sport? → E2 Sports, Fitness & Recreation
42. Protective equipment worn against a work or workshop hazard (hard hat, safety glasses, respirator, ear defenders, hi-vis, cut-resistant clothing)? → C1 Tools & Workshop Equipment
43. Footwear? → A2 Footwear
44. A garment, headwear, scarf, glove, belt, hosiery, uniform, costume or traditional dress? → A1 Clothing
45. An ornament worn on the body, hair or clothing? → A3 Jewellery
46. A bag, wallet or small leather good, eyewear frame or sunglasses, luggage, umbrella, hand fan, baby carrier or other carried accessory? → A4 Bags & Accessories
47. A fragrance worn on the body, or a bottle, sample or material for it? → H4 Fragrance
48. Made to be used on the body for grooming, hygiene, cosmetics or comfort? → H1 Personal Care & Beauty
49. A material, tool or machine for making things by hand (paint, paper, fabric, yarn, beads, clay, glass, leather, model paints)? → C4 Craft & Art Supplies
50. Made for growing plants, keeping gardens, grounds and pools, or cooking and heating outdoors? → C2 Garden & Grounds
51. Made for writing, paper and desk work, or calculating? → C5 Office & Stationery
52. Made to prepare, cook, brew, serve or store food and drink? → B5 Kitchen & Dining
53. Made to clean the home or its textiles, or to collect waste? → B6 Cleaning & Laundry
54. A movable appliance that heats, cools, moves, cleans or dries a room's air? → B7 Portable Climate & Air
55. Movable equipment made to secure or protect a home and its people, or to keep pests out? → B8 Home Safety & Security
56. A movable light, bulb, shade or lighting part? → B3 Lighting
57. Movable furniture or storage? → B1 Furniture & Storage
58. A household textile (rug, bedding, cushion, curtain, blind, towel, table linen)? → B2 Soft Furnishings
59. Made to decorate a home or garden, or for a celebration effect? → B4 Decor
60. A tool, instrument or machine made to cut, shape, join, measure, lift, power or repair? → C1 Tools & Workshop Equipment
61. A building material, hardware item or supply bought loose (timber, masonry, paint, plumbing, electrical, fixings, adhesives, packing, batteries, fuel)? → C8 Building Materials & Hardware
62. None of the above? → hold and log for review

A1.test: a garment, headwear, scarf, glove, belt, hosiery, uniform, costume or traditional dress worn on the body for everyday, formal or work wear.
prec: Garments, footwear and helmets made for one sport are E2; motorcycle riding gear is G1.
Protective equipment worn against a work hazard (hard hats, respirators, hi-vis, chainsaw trousers) is C1.
Religious dress and vestments, fetish wear and toy dress-up crowns and wands: A1, A1 and E1.
Wigs, hairpieces and hair ties are H1.

A2.test: anything worn on the foot, including work, riding and traditional footwear, with shoe care.
prec: Footwear made for one sport (football boots, ski boots, climbing shoes) is E2.
Shoe polish and shoe care are A2, not B6; orthotic insoles made to treat are H2.

A3.test: an ornament worn on the body, hair or clothing, including amulets, piercing jewellery, traditional jewellery and jewellery parts.
prec: Smart rings are D2; medical ID jewellery is H2; watches are A5.
Plain hair ties and clips are H1; loose gemstones and pearls are F6; patches sold to sew on are C4.

A4.test: a bag, wallet, small leather good, eyewear frame or sunglasses, luggage, umbrella, hand fan, baby carrier or other accessory carried on the person.
prec: All frames, sunglasses and reading glasses are A4; spectacle and contact lenses are H2.
A case made for one object follows it; tool bags are C1; cool bags B5.
Quivers, chalk bags and hydration packs are E2; sword canes are E4.

A5.test: a watch, clock or timer whose main function is to show or measure time, with its straps, storage and parts.
prec: Smartwatches and hybrid smartwatches are D2; clock radios and smart displays D3.
Chess and game clocks are E1; kitchen timers B5; a garden sundial is B4.

B1.test: movable furniture made to sit, lie, work at, display or store things, indoors or out, including nursery furniture, racks, boxes and organisers.
prec: Fitted kitchens, wardrobes and other fitted storage are G3.
Workbenches and tool storage are C1; camp chairs and tables are E2; desk organisers C5.
Albums and binders for collected objects follow what they hold (F3, F5).

B2.test: a household textile: rug or mat, bedding, blanket, cushion, curtain or blind, towel, or table and kitchen linen.
prec: Fitted flooring is G3; a hair towel is H1; furnishing fabric sold by the metre to sew is B2.

B3.test: a movable light (lamp, ceiling or wall light, decorative or outdoor light, torch, lantern) or a bulb, strip, shade or lamp part.
prec: Built-in fittings (recessed downlights, track, under-cabinet) are G3.
Candles and candle holders are B4; studio and photo lights D4; grow lights C2; aquarium lights B10.

B4.test: an object made to decorate a home or garden, or a celebration effect: vases, mirrors, wall decor, candles, home fragrance, incense, seasonal and folk decor, fireworks, artificial plants, garden ornaments, flags.
prec: Decorative lighting is B3; works of art and collectible figurines are F2.
Incense made for a rite is F4; perfume worn on the body is H4.
Decorative replica weapons are E4.

B5.test: an object made to prepare, cook, brew, serve or store food and drink: cookware, kitchen knives, tools, appliances, coffee and tea equipment, tableware, glassware, preserving gear.
prec: Barbecues, smokers and pizza ovens are C2; camp stoves E2.
Built-in and range cookers, fitted sinks and built-in wine cabinets are G3; freestanding ones stay B5.
Pocket and utility knives are C1; fighting and hunting knives E4.

B6.test: equipment, tools and products made to clean a home or its textiles, or to collect waste.
prec: Shoe care is A2; vehicle care G1; adult-product cleaners H3; pool cleaners C2.
Central vacuum and waste disposal units are G3; aquarium cleaning tools B10.

B7.test: a movable appliance that heats, cools, moves, cleans, humidifies or dries the air of a room, or monitors indoor air quality.
prec: Built-in heating, cooling, ventilation, ceiling fans and heated towel rails are G3.
Patio heaters and fire pits are C2; electric blankets B2; heated low tables B1.

B8.test: a movable object made to secure a home, its people and its contents, or to keep pests out: locks, safes, alarm kits, cameras, doorbells, fire and leak detectors, child safety, pest control.
prec: Door and window locks, multipoint and smart locks included, are B8.
Installed intruder alarms, intercoms and window guards are G3; bicycle and vehicle locks G1.
Skin-applied insect repellent is H1; GPS pet trackers B10.

B10.test: equipment, food and supplies made to keep, feed, house, carry, train or care for animals, by animal (dogs, cats, fish and ponds, horses, birds, small animals, reptiles, bees).
prec: The animals themselves are in the breeds and species register.
Farm-scale livestock equipment is C7; backyard flocks and leisure horses stay B10.
Riders' helmets are E2 and riding boots A2; pet urns F4.

C1.test: a tool, instrument or machine made to cut, shape, join, measure, lift, power or repair, or protective equipment worn against a work hazard.
prec: Pocket, EDC and bushcraft knives, multi-tools, axes and hand log splitters are C1.
Tractor-driven splitters and sawmills are C7; chainsaws C2; vehicle jacks and axle stands G1.
Building and trade measuring tools are C1; observing and weather instruments E6.

C2.test: equipment and supplies made for growing plants or keeping gardens, grounds and pools, or for cooking and heating outdoors.
prec: Living plants and seeds are C3; garden furniture B1; garden ornaments B4.
Garden buildings, in-ground pools and built-in outdoor kitchens are G3; above-ground and inflatable pools C2.
Landscaping stone and aggregates are C8.

C3.test: a living plant, fungus or culture kept to grow or propagate, a fresh-cut ornamental plant or Christmas tree, or a seed, bulb, spore or cutting for growing.
prec: Cut produce and herbs sold to eat are J4; a plant sold still growing is C3.
Dried and artificial plants are B4; dried baking yeast is J5.

C4.test: a material, tool or machine for making things by hand, grouped by material: paint, paper, fabric, yarn, beads, clay, glass, resin, wax, leather, model paints.
prec: Writing pens and pencils are C5; model kits E1; finished candles B4.
Woodworking and metalworking tools are C1; craft stamps C4, office rubber stamps C5.

C5.test: an object made for writing, paper and desk work or calculating: pens, ink, notebooks, paper, seals and stamps, filing, calculators, collector machines (typewriters, slide rules).
prec: Printers and scanners are D1; packing materials C8; storage boxes B1.

C7.test: machinery and equipment made for farm, smallholding or woodland production: tractors and implements, vintage tractors and stationary engines, farm-scale machines, livestock equipment.
prec: Lawn and garden tractors and ride-on mowers are C2.
Beekeeping is B10; equipment for a few backyard hens or leisure horses is B10.

C8.test: a raw building supply, hardware item or household consumable bought loose: timber, masonry, heritage materials, stone, fencing, paint, plumbing, electrical, fixings, adhesives, packing, batteries, fuel.
prec: A finished fitting installed in a home (door, window, tap, switch, fitted floor) is G3.
Pocket lighters are J10; utility lighters and matches C8.
Battery packs for one tool platform are C1; standard cells C8.

D1.test: a computer, its components, storage, monitors and peripherals, printers and 3D printers, networking, cables and hubs, security keys, enthusiast keyboards, or maker electronics.
prec: Consoles, handheld gaming PCs and VR headsets are E5.
Speech microphones are D1; music microphones and audio interfaces E3.
An electronic toy made for play, such as a coding robot, is E1.

D2.test: a phone, tablet, e-reader, wearable (smartwatch, fitness band, smart ring, smart glasses), organiser, navigator, tracker, or two-way or amateur radio.
prec: A watch whose main display is the time is A5; GPS pet trackers B10.
Electronics fitted to a vehicle (car audio, dashcam, mounted sat-nav) are G1.

D3.test: equipment for listening to sound or watching pictures: headphones, loudspeakers, turntables, hi-fi, portable players, radios, TVs, projectors, video players, smart speakers and displays.
prec: Studio, stage and DJ gear is E3; records and discs F1.

D4.test: a camera, lens, flash, studio light, tripod, film or darkroom item, or another accessory for taking or making photographs and video.
prec: Security cameras are B8; dashcams G1; telescope and astro cameras E6.

E1.test: an object made for play or a hobby model, or for a game played at a table or with cards, dice, tiles or tokens, or a science-discovery kit.
prec: Board and card games are filed as objects; their titles are out of scope.
Toy blasters and swords are E1; airsoft and paintball E2; real weapons E4.
A single-line play kite is E1; sport and traction kites E2. Card sleeves and deck boxes are E1.

E2.test: equipment made for a sport, fitness, dance or outdoor recreation, including camping, fishing and hunting accessories and garments, footwear and helmets made for one sport.
prec: Bows, firearms and hunting knives are E4; quivers, calls, decoys and tree stands E2.
Cycling helmets and clothing are E2; bicycles and their components G1.
Garden trampolines are E1; fitness trampolines E2; cool boxes B5.

E3.test: a musical instrument of any tradition, its parts and cases, or gear for amplifying, effects, recording, live sound or DJing.
prec: Toy instruments are E1; listening headphones and speakers D3; game guitar controllers E5.

E4.test: a weapon for fighting, self-defence, hunting or target shooting (swords, fighting knives, firearms, air guns, bows, polearms), its ammunition, sights and parts, armour, or a deactivated or replica weapon.
prec: Kitchen knives are B5; pocket, EDC and bushcraft knives C1.
Fencing, HEMA and training weapons are E2; toy weapons E1.

E5.test: video-game hardware: consoles and handhelds, game media as objects, controllers, accessories, modding and repair, VR and XR headsets, arcade cabinets and pinball machines.
prec: Game titles are out of scope; in-game items are I2; game subscriptions I3.
Toys-to-life figures are E1; their portal is E5.

E6.test: an instrument made to observe the sky, nature or the very small, or to measure weather and the Earth: telescopes, binoculars, microscopes, magnifiers, weather instruments, sky models, historic instruments, home lab.
prec: Rifle scopes are E4; low-vision magnifiers H2; science toys E1.
Trade measuring tools are C1; indoor air-quality monitors B7; kitchen thermometers B5.

F1.test: a published work fixed on a physical carrier (book, record, disc, tape, film, comic, periodical, sheet music, map, globe), filed by carrier and edition, with storage made for media.
prec: Video-game media is E5; software on disc I1; home recordings F5.
Copies of sacred texts and ritual scrolls are F4.

F2.test: an original or editioned work of art (painting, drawing, print, photograph, sculpture, studio ceramics or glass, textile art, calligraphy) or a collectible ornamental figurine.
prec: Character, action and designer figures are E1; garden statues B4.
Vases and decorative glass by a factory or house are B4; studio pieces by an artist are F2.
A photograph issued as an edition or signed as a work is F2; other prints F5.

F3.test: money, bullion, a stamp or postal item, a collected trading card, token, medal, order or decoration, trophy or award, or a holder, slab or album made for them.
prec: Payment, transit and phone cards and share certificates are F5.
Ceremonial regalia and insignia of office are F4.
A casino-issued chip is F3; a home poker chip set E1.

F4.test: an object made for worship, devotion, divination or mourning, or as ceremonial regalia: images and altars, prayer aids, scriptures and holders, ritual vessels, light and incense, tarot, funeral goods.
prec: Ornaments worn as amulets are A3; religious dress A1.
Festival decorations (Christmas, Diwali, Halloween) are B4; burial plots G2.

F5.test: a personal or collected paper or card: letters, autographs, manuscripts, photographs, postcards, ephemera, shares and bonds, payment, transit and phone cards, identity and legal papers.
prec: Published works are F1; banknotes F3; card holders and passport covers A4.
A pass as a right of access is I3; the card kept or collected is F5.

F6.test: a natural object, not made by people beyond cleaning, cutting, polishing or preserving, kept as a specimen: minerals, gemstones, fossils, meteorites, rocks, shells, taxidermy, element samples, and their display domes.
prec: A set gemstone is A3; a stone worked as a shrine object F4.
Stone, gravel and firewood sold for use are C8.

G1.test: a vehicle made to move people or goods (car, motorcycle, bicycle, van, caravan, boat, aircraft, heritage rail, horse-drawn, pram), its parts, motorcycle riding gear, or vehicle care.
prec: Tractors are C7; ride-on mowers C2; boards, skates, skis and kick scooters E2; ride-on toys E1.
Houseboats, static caravans and tiny homes kept as dwellings are G2.

G2.test: real property as a whole: land and estates, houses and flats, factory-built, mobile and floating homes, unusual conversions, or a burial place.
prec: Garden buildings, garages and other structures within a property are G3.
Commercial and industrial buildings are out of scope.

G3.test: a part built into or fixed to a home or grounds, or a home system: fitted kitchens, bathrooms, saunas and hot tubs, fireplaces, doors, stairs, floors, heating, water, power, controls, built-in lights, garden buildings.
prec: Saunas and hot tubs are G3 in every form, portable and inflatable included; baby baths are H1.
Raw supplies bought loose are C8; door and window locks B8.
Movable appliances and lights stay in Home (B); installed mobility aids (stairlifts, grab bars) are G3.

H1.test: a product or tool used on the body for grooming, hygiene, cosmetics or comfort: skincare, make-up, hair, shaving, oral care, bath and body, intimate care, massage.
prec: Products that treat a condition are H2; fragrance H4; towels B2.
Personal lubricant is H1; sex toys and their cleaners H3.

H2.test: an object made to diagnose, treat, monitor or compensate for illness, injury or disability, or for contraception, fertility, pregnancy or first aid: medicines, supplements, monitors, mobility, hearing and vision aids.
prec: Frames and reading glasses are A4; spectacle and contact lenses H2.
Stairlifts and grab bars are G3; protein bars J8; fitness trackers D2.

H3.test: an object made for sexual stimulation or for restraint during sexual activity, with its care and storage, described neutrally.
prec: Lingerie and fetish wear are A1; contraceptives H2; personal lubricant H1.

H4.test: a fragrance worn on the body (perfume, attar, mist, solid perfume), its samples and decants, bottles and atomisers, and perfumery materials.
prec: Home fragrance, diffusers and incense are B4; deodorant H1.

I1.test: a program, app or hosted tool valued for what the program does for its owner, however licensed or delivered, including a paid licence or unlock.
prec: A hosted service valued for storage, connection or a catalogue is I3; medical apps H2.

I2.test: an item that exists only as data and is held as a file, entitlement or token: fonts, creative assets, game and platform items, personal media files, domains, NFTs.
prec: Cryptocurrency holdings and titles are out of scope; prints of personal photos are F5.

I3.test: a recurring plan, membership, pass or retained service: streaming, reading, games and learning, online services, phone and internet, clubs and passes, subscription boxes, services and staff.
prec: One-off services and single-event tickets are out of scope.
Where a plan gives access to software or an asset, the plan is I3 and the item I1 or I2.

J1.test: meat, poultry and game as bought, fresh or preserved (cuts, hams, cured meats, sausages, deli, tinned meats), and meat alternatives.
prec: Ready meals containing meat are J5; tofu and tempeh J3; pet food B10.

J2.test: fish and seafood as bought: fresh and frozen fish, shellfish (live ones sold to eat included), smoked, tinned, salted and dried fish, caviar and roe, fish cakes and surimi.
prec: Fish sauce and other condiments are J5; living ornamental fish go to the animal register.

J3.test: milk, cream, butter and ghee, yoghurt and fermented milks, cheese, eggs, infant and toddler milks, plant alternatives to them, and tofu, tempeh and yuba.
prec: Ice cream is J8; plant-only fat spreads J5; medical nutrition H2.

J4.test: fresh or frozen fruit, vegetables, salad, herbs, mushrooms and sea vegetables, sold to eat, not dried, tinned or prepared.
prec: Dried fruit and vegetables are J5; a plant sold still growing is C3.

J5.test: any other food bought to cook with or eat: oils, grains, pasta, pulses, flour, sugar, spices, sauces, preserves, dried fruit, spreads, home-brew ingredients, and packaged prepared and frozen foods.
prec: Packaged ready meals, pizza, soups, dips and baby food are J5 whatever they contain.
Snack nuts are J8; tofu J3; cocoa powder J6; baking chocolate J8.

J6.test: coffee, tea, cocoa and drinking chocolate, and herbal and fruit infusions, as beans, leaves, powders, pods or bags to brew or mix.
prec: Ready-to-drink coffee and tea are J9; brewing equipment B5.

J7.test: an alcoholic drink in a sealed container (wine, beer, whisky, spirits, liqueurs, sake, cider, mead, ready-to-drink mixes), and no- and low-alcohol versions of them.
prec: Kombucha and other fermented soft drinks are J9.

J8.test: bought bread and bakery, biscuits and crackers, chocolate, sweets and confectionery, crisps and savoury snacks, snack nuts and bars, and ice cream.
prec: Unbaked dough and baking ingredients are J5; protein powders H2.

J9.test: a bought non-alcoholic drink ready to drink or dilute: water, sodas, tonics and mixers, juices, syrups and cordials, fermented soft drinks, energy and sports drinks, ready-to-drink coffee and tea.
prec: Milk drinks and plant drinks are J3; maple and golden syrups J5; cannabis drinks J10.

J10.test: tobacco, nicotine, cannabis and other plant products taken for effect (cigars, pipes, cigarettes, vapes, snus, shisha, kratom), and gear to smoke, vape, light and store them.
prec: Nicotine and cannabis medicines sold to treat are H2; living cannabis plants C3.
Utility lighters and matches are C8; herbal teas J6.
